name: Elyse Marrone
headline: Registered dietitian, functional and integrative nutrition
on_the_show: Elyse described herself as a functionally and integratively trained dietitian who looks at all seven pillars of a patient’s lifestyle: food first, exercise, sleep, stress management, supplementation, hydration and community. She calls the goal the triple HD plan. After a breast cancer diagnosis, she said, the first place she looks is the gut, where she puts 80 to 90% of the immune system. She closed on sleep, recommending blue light blocker glasses from 8 o’clock in the evening to help the body start producing melatonin.
on_the_show_quote: I want to be healthy, healthy, healthy, dead.

background.text: She is a licensed and registered dietitian/nutritionist and a certified gluten-free practitioner (CGP).

She completed her undergraduate degree at the University of Massachusetts Amherst, and her clinical internship and graduate training at UMass Medical Center in Worcester through Framingham State University.
She has trained in functional medicine and nutritional biochemistry through the Institute for Functional Medicine (IFM) and the American Academy for Anti-Aging Medicine (A4M).
She is a member of the Dietitians in Functional Medicine practice group.
She lectures on nutrition topics at universities, medical offices and other venues for practitioners, students, patients and the public.
Her practice’s site says she has more than twenty years of experience in the field of nutrition.

research_notes: Identity confirmed: own site thenutritioninstitute.org was named on air, carries the same phone number given on air, and lists a Jupiter address (2055 Military Trail #304). Credentials as written on her own bio page: 'RD/LDN CGP' (no comma); the transcript header writes 'RD/LDN, CGP'. Same meaning, pick one style for display. Location conflict on her own site: the address and on-air statement say Jupiter, but the site's body copy and page titles still say 'private practice in Palm Beach Gardens'. Used Jupiter (address + what she said on air). On air she also said she works with chiropractor Dr. Paula Newmark at Back to Health in Jupiter; not verified on the web, left out of background. Instagram link on her site is written 'Elysemarrone' (Instagram handles are case-insensitive); the Instagram profile itself was not opened. The bio page is also served at the-lifestyle-nutrition-institute.ueniweb.com (same content); the canonical thenutritioninstitute.org URL returns 200 and carries the UMass text. Her site mentions peptide and exosome 'regenerative therapies'; deliberately left out as a clinical claim.
